hints: Begin with the compound-angle identity for $\cos(2\theta+\theta)$.
Use $\sin^2\theta=1-\cos^2\theta$, then collect the cubic and linear terms in $\cos\theta$.
walkthrough:
Expand $\cos(2\theta + \theta)$ using the compound angle identity $\cos(A + B) = \cos A\cos B - \sin A\sin B$:
$$\cos 3\theta = \cos(2\theta + \theta) = \cos 2\theta\cos\theta - \sin 2\theta\sin\theta$$

hints: Use the identity from part (a) and express $\cos2\theta$ in terms of $\cos\theta$ so the equation contains one trigonometric function.
Bring all terms to one side and factor out $\cos\theta$ before solving the remaining quadratic in $\cos\theta$.
Include $\theta=90^\circ$ from $\cos\theta=0$, then find the single angle in $0^\circ\le\theta\le180^\circ$ for each admissible quadratic root.
Give the non-exact angles to $0.1^\circ$ and reject values outside the stated degree interval.
walkthrough:
Substitute the identity $\cos 3\theta = 4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta$ and $\cos 2\theta = 2\cos^2\theta - 1$ into the equation:
$$(4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta) + \cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1) = \cos^2\theta$$

Expand and collect all terms on one side:
$$4\cos^3\theta - 3\cos\theta + 2\cos^3\theta - \cos\theta - \cos^2\theta = 0$$
$$6\cos^3\theta - \cos^2\theta - 4\cos\theta = 0$$

Solve the quadratic factor $6\cos^2\theta - \cos\theta - 4 = 0$ using the quadratic formula:
$$\cos\theta = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{(-1)^2 - 4(6)(-4)}}{2(6)} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{97}}{12}$$

Calculate the root from the positive branch $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{97}}{12} \approx 0.90407$:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(0.90407) \approx 25.3^\circ$$

Calculate the root from the negative branch $\cos\theta = \dfrac{1 - \sqrt{97}}{12} \approx -0.73740$:
$$\theta = \cos^{-1}(-0.73740) \approx 137.5^\circ$$
